newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland partly lifts mining lease freeze.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland partly lifts mining lease freeze.

text.p: The Queensland state government said on Thursday it would partially lift a freeze on mining exploration permits and leasehold development, halted because of compensation fears arising from a controversial High Court ruling.
The issue and renewal of most mining leases in Queensland as well as all land dealing and leasehold property development were suspended in January, following the ruling on native title.
"The state government is prepared to acccept reasonable risk to avoid a gridlock in land management," Premier Rob Borbidge told a press conference.

Borbidge said Queensland had determined it would accept risk to ensure pastoral, mining and commercial activities could proceed "to the greatest extent possible in the face of the Wik decision of the High Court."

In a case brought by several north Queensland Aboriginal groups including the Wik people, the High Court ruled last December that native title could co-exist with state pastoral leases held by farmers and in many cases, mining companies which had mine leases on pastoral leases.
Borbidge said today's decision would free up many, but not all, earlier frozen land dealings.

Renewals of 254 mining leases, 94 mining claims and a petroleum lease would be processed as soon as possible as well as a further 155 mining leases and 100 mining claims expected to mature this year, Borbidge said.
